name: Ruth Spencer
life: “I still remember receiving spare batteries for a radio I never switched off.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Ruth by a small Saturday habit. Ruth can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I saved his old radio when he moved. It still gets the away matches better than my phone.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a narrow brass watch set a little fast. Ruth has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. Ruth raises one eyebrow long before saying yes during a conversation.
personality: Ruth tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Ruth will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
family: Tait Wynn is Ruth’s cousin raised in the same household. Ruth chooses whether to use it. Tait saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The last green*, Tait says, “He told me to get a proper job when I was a kid.”
connections: Toby Hsu. An old scarf and a working away-match radio let two neighbors bring the club home.

reactions.situation: The widower asks for a Sunday with no appointments
reactions.response: Ruth keeps necessary care covered and leaves the social part of Sunday open.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Ruth offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Ruth repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
